handbookNote: Oregon Commercial Driver License Manual (base AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' content, version March 2025), published by the Oregon Department of Transportation (ODOT), Driver and Motor Vehicle Services (DMV) Division -- the SAME agency/division that publishes Oregon's non-commercial Driver Manual already built in this project (oregon.gov/odot/dmv); Oregon does not split CDL testing into a separate agency or division. Fetched directly from the official PDF at https://www.oregon.gov/odot/Forms/DMV/36m.pdf on 2026-08-23 (12.6MB PDF, linked as 'Commercial Driver Manual' from the official DMV Manuals & Publications page at https://www.oregon.gov/odot/dmv/pages/form/manuals.aspx), full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/or_cdl_research/or_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,086 lines, cross-referenced against the official online-manual page https://www.oregon.gov/odot/dmv/pages/online_cdl_manual_2/section_i.aspx (checked 2026-08-23). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Exam mechanics are HEDGED, and for a genuinely structural reason rather than mere non-disclosure: Oregon's own manual (Section i - Oregon Information, 'Knowledge Testing Information') states commercial knowledge tests are given on a touch-screen and explicitly says 'Once enough questions have been answered to determine a pass or fail, the test will be terminated' -- i.e. Oregon's CDL knowledge tests are adaptive/computer-terminated rather than a fixed-length battery, so there is NO single official 'number of questions' to report for any Oregon CDL knowledge test, general or endorsement. The manual also never states a passing-score percentage anywhere in the fetched text (confirmed by exhaustive keyword search for 'percent', '80%', 'passing score', and similar terms). The federally standardized 80% minimum under 49 CFR 383.135(a) applies regardless, and third-party CDL test-prep aggregators (not used as a source for any question content) converge on a conventional '50 questions/80%' General Knowledge format consistent with the shared AAMVA base manual used by other CDL-track states in this project, but this specific item count is NOT asserted as an officially confirmed Oregon figure anywhere in this question bank. What IS confirmed directly from Oregon's own manual: commercial knowledge tests are English-only (no interpreters), untimed (other than needing to finish before the office closes), retakeable as early as the same day, and scores are valid for six months; the CDL skills test has three segments (vehicle inspection, basic control skills, road test) all normally completed the same day, requires a CLP held at least 14 days beforehand, and skills-test results are valid for six months. The manual also contains an internal inconsistency, resolved rather than silently picked: Section i's Oregon-specific front matter states a first violation of an out-of-service order costs a driver their CDL for 'at least 180 days,' while Section 1's generic AAMVA-boilerplate text renders the same first-offense figure as '[For at least 90 days' with a stray bracket -- a redline/tracked-changes artifact, not clean prose (verified directly in the extracted PDF text, line 845 vs. lines 369-370). This question bank uses the unambiguous, non-bracketed Oregon-specific 180-day figure from Section i as authoritative, consistent with how this project has resolved similar AAMVA-boilerplate artifacts in other states' manuals (e.g. Louisiana's tracked-changes '90 180 days' rendering). Oregon uses the standard federal three-class system (Class A/B/C, no NM-style fourth class) and the standard six CDL endorsements (H, N, P, T, X, S); the manual's own Section 1 text states 'There are six kinds of CDL endorsements.' Oregon-specific administrative detail confirmed from the manual's front matter: ELDT (Entry Level Driver Training) required before a first Class A/B CDL, a B-to-A upgrade, or a first Passenger/School Bus endorsement, and before a first Hazardous Materials endorsement knowledge test; CDL age minimums 18 intrastate / 21 interstate; hazmat endorsement requires a TSA fingerprint-based security background check; a DOT medical exam via a National-Registry-listed examiner, with a Medical Examiner's Certificate valid up to two years; a military CDL skills-test waiver; Oregon's own Move-Over Law (move over one lane, or slow to 5 mph below the posted limit, for any vehicle with flashing/hazard lights on the shoulder); human-trafficking and diversion rules specific to Oregon commercial driving privileges; and a hardship-permit rule that explicitly excludes commercial vehicle operation. Content-depth rationale: Oregon uses the AAMVA-authored 'Modernized Testing System' base manual (version March 2025, a notably newer base-content revision than several other CDL-track states in this project, e.g. Kentucky's September 2022 or Louisiana/New Mexico's July 2017 versions), organized into the same 13 core sections plus Oregon-specific front matter -- Section i Oregon Information, Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split here into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering 2.1 Vehicle Inspection through 2.16 Mountain Driving, 03_driving_safely_b covering 2.17 Driving Emergencies through 2.23 Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering 9.1 Intent of the Regulations through 9.4 Loading and Unloading, 11_hazmat_b covering 9.5 Bulk Packaging Marking through 9.7 Hazardous Materials Emergencies, explicitly excluding the 9.8 Glossary since the manual states test-takers 'will not be tested on this glossary'), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection Test, and Section 12 Basic Control Skills Test combined with Section 13 On-road Driving into one bucket -- plus Oregon-specific administrative detail (eligibility, ELDT, medical/HME requirements, testing procedures, fees, skills-test structure, out-of-service/human-trafficking/diversion/hardship-permit rules, Move-Over Law) layered into the licensing bucket from the manual's Section i and Section 1 front matter. Sections 3 (Cargo), 7 (Doubles/Triples), and 8 (Tank Vehicles) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly (25, 26, and 16 questions respectively) rather than padded to match larger sections; Section 2 (Driving Safely, split across two buckets totaling 162 questions) and Section 9 (Hazardous Materials, split across two buckets totaling 105 questions) supported deeper coverage and were sized up accordingly. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Oregon manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers -- all numeric specifications (air brake PSI thresholds and leak-rate limits, tire tread depth minimums, hazmat placard weight/size thresholds, school bus danger-zone and tail-swing distances, stopping-distance and following-distance figures, disqualification day/year counts) were verified against the actual Oregon manual text read during drafting, cross-checked by the top-level agent against the source PDF independently of each drafting sub-agent's self-reported citations.
